proposal.summary: Marcus's only affected job is J1 (drain cleaning, 13:00-14:00). Plumber Aisha Khan (T6) can reach 9 Harbor St from her 31 Birch Ave job by 12:42 and keep the 13:00 slot with no revenue at risk, so this is a reassignment with no delay and no side effects.
assumptions: J1 is the only job Marcus (T1) loses; his other jobs are none, and J1 is the only T1 job in the data.
T6 finishes J11 at 12:15 as scheduled, despite the property manager being on site.
Travel from J11's location (31 Birch Ave) to J1 is 27 minutes, per the travel_minutes matrix.

jobs.rationale: Urgency ties at standard, so job revenue decides the order; T6 is the only qualified technician who can keep the 13:00 slot, arriving at 12:42. On the revenue_protected criterion, T6 puts no revenue at risk because the next job (J12 at 15:00) still starts after the 14:19 return from J1.

alternatives.tradeoff: Priya finishes J3 at 13:00 and needs 28 minutes to reach Harbor St, so J1 slips 28 minutes; this is within the standard 240-minute limit but disrupts the customer for no benefit.
